findings.claim: The contrastive half of key B ("rather than in anything the zoo buys") is in literal tension with the very sentence the rationale cites as its anchor, because the passage explicitly makes labor the thing the money buys.
findings.evidence: Passage closing line: "The budget line is called enrichment; what it mostly buys is labor." Key B: "That the expense lies mainly in the keepers' hours rather than in anything the zoo buys." Rationale: "closes on 'The budget line is called enrichment; what it mostly buys is labor.' Putting those together gives B: the real expense is staff time, not equipment." Read strictly, keepers' hours ARE labor and labor IS what the passage says the budget buys, so B's own phrasing negates the sentence that supports it. The language stage had this exact clause under the lens — candidates/ -> candidates-corrected/ rewrote "falls mainly on the keepers' hours rather than on anything the zoo buys" to "lies mainly in ... rather than in ..." and left "anything the zoo buys" untouched.
findings.why: Not verdict-changing and not a double key: the natural reading of "anything the zoo buys" is goods/equipment (the passage's paradox is precisely that a goods budget funds hours), and no other option is closer — A is contradicted, C requires 'ordinary keeping duties', D compares to alternatives the passage never names. Recorded because it is the one phrase a literal-minded complaining student could quote back, and it is exactly the passage/option cross-check the integrated stage owns.

findings.claim: The MAJOR world-knowledge shortcut G-STEM recorded is still fully present in the shipped file, and no review record shows any stage adjudicated it; the gate's quoted evidence is also stale relative to the shipped option text.
findings.evidence: verdicts.jsonl / verdicts-gstem.jsonl, G-STEM q:1, verdict "flag", severity major: "WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick B): it is well known in zoo husbandry that enrichment objects are cheap (boxes, sacks, browse) and that staff time is the real cost, so a domain-aware reader leans to B." Its quote is the pre-language-edit wording "That the expense falls mainly on the keepers' hours rather than on anything the zoo buys.", which no longer exists in candidates-final/ ("lies mainly in ... in ..."), and G-STEM was not re-run after that edit. Independent blind re-test on the options alone (blind/elf-b11-004.json) reproduces the lean: of four substantive cost claims, B is the genre-conventional 'the real cost is staff time' reveal, and reviews/pedagogy.jsonl carries only {"verdict":"MINOR_FIXES"} with no findings field.
findings.why: Explicitly NOT a refutation: the gate caught it, report.json carries the unit as SURVIVED_FLAGGED, the runbook's post-option-edit re-gate set is mech + blind G-KEY x2 + G-DISTRACTOR (G-STEM re-run not required), and my own blind pass agrees with the gate's classification — A, B and D are all substantive cost claims, so the leak is domain knowledge rather than form (only C is genre-eliminable). Noted because the construct-validity risk and the accepted mitigation live only in a gate line whose quote no longer matches the shipping text.

findings.claim: The three review records for this unit are verdict-only, so the recorded verdicts cannot be falsified from the records themselves; I audited the artifacts instead, and the artifacts do substantiate each verdict.
findings.evidence: reviews/{language,pedagogy,integrated}.jsonl lines for elf-b11-004 carry only keys candidate_id, stage, verdict, reviewed_by, date — no findings. Artifact trail instead: candidates/ -> candidates-corrected/ shows the language work ("Working For It" -> "Working for It" title-case fix; "falls mainly on ... rather than on" -> "lies mainly in ... rather than in"), consistent with CORRECTED; candidates-corrected/ -> candidates-final/ shows a substantive factual repair of the rationale's A-refutation, from "the materials named (bark, a crevice, almonds) are conspicuously cheap" (loose: bark and the crevice are the WILD foraging problem the devices resemble, not materials the zoo owns) to "the only equipment the passage names is a puzzle box baited with almonds, and the wild problems it echoes (bark to be stripped, a narrow crevice) are found, not bought", consistent with MINOR_FIXES / MINOR_NOTES.
findings.why: Record-format observation only. Everything else checks out on my own pass: all quoted strings in the rationale are verbatim in the shipped text ("take a keeper twenty minutes to prepare each morning", "The budget line is called enrichment; what it mostly buys is labor.", 'ordinary keeping duties', 'tend to', 'mainly'); the anti-tell claims hold (by the pipeline's own token measure in gates/scripts/mech.py, C=15 < B=16 < A=18 = D=18, so B is second-shortest and not longest); trap labels match the ELF-TYPE-002 taxonomy in elf/families.json (A = outside_knowledge, D = "Tva-stegs-hopp"); AmE is held throughout student-facing text with no BrE forms, straight apostrophes and spaced em dashes matching corpus convention; and the key is uniquely defensible — C fails on "ordinary keeping duties" (preparing devices is enrichment work), D on alternatives the passage never names, A on an economics claim the text never makes.
